findings.title: Concurrency test can pass without catching the NPE
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a reader thread and then immediately deletes every group and sets deletedAll before asserting caughtExceptions is empty, without joining the reader or ensuring it has entered groups(). On a fast run the reader may not be scheduled until after deletedAll is already true, so the loop never calls the admin API and the assertion passes without exercising GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount. If a list call is in flight when deletedAll is set, the main thread can also assert before that call throws and the exception is added to caughtExceptions, so a reproduced NPE is ignored. The regression test therefore does not reliably fail if the concurrent-delete NPE returns.

findings.title: Reader thread shares the admin client and outlives the test
findings.body: The background thread calls managedRealm.admin().groups() in a tight loop while the test thread deletes groups through the same admin client, and the thread is never joined, interrupted, or marked daemon. The Keycloak admin client and its JAX-RS/HTTP client are not safe for concurrent use, so the two threads can corrupt in-flight requests and produce exceptions unrelated to the cache NPE (or hide it). Because the thread is not stopped before the test method returns, it can still be issuing list calls against the shared realm while later tests run, causing cross-test interference or a non-daemon thread that keeps the suite from exiting if a request hangs.
